title: Failure-mode: gate-inverting hook edit — set -e + pipeline + missing-file stack read a RED gate as green (Evergreen 1e6b10; caught + amended pre-push)
body:
Observation: a pre-commit hook edit (tee of the gate output for flake-evidence preservation) silently INVERTED the gate — a commit landed locally while the turbo gate was red (2 failed tasks). Caught minutes later by reading the teed log itself; the broken commit was amended green BEFORE any push (local-broken-code-never-leaves held).

Diagnosis (three stacked defects, each individually quiet): (1) a pipeline reports only its last stage's exit, so { gate; echo "$?" > status; } | tee loses the gate's code to tee's 0; (2) husky runs hooks under sh -e, so the bare failing gate aborted the group BEFORE the capture echo ran — the status file was never written; (3) [ "$(cat missing-file)" -ne 0 ] is a test ERROR, and an if-statement reads a test error as FALSE — absent evidence parsed as success.

Cure (proven under sh -e three ways — blocks on red, passes on green, fails closed on absent status): pre-truncate the status file; write it via gate && echo 0 || echo 1 (set -e tolerates handled failures); default an absent/empty read to failure (cat ... 2>/dev/null || echo 1); compare as strings, never numerically. Generalises: ANY exit-code capture inside a hook must be designed against set -e AND pipeline semantics AND missing-file reads, and the negative case must be demonstrated, not assumed.

Pointer: the 3a PR (fix/lifecycle-lease-timer-race, commit 918f022b9) carries the fixed shape + full disclosure; handoff record 2026-06-11-evergreen-reliability-seat-to-n3-team.md carries the context. Same family as the piped-exit and green-verifier-without-count lessons in distilled.md.
